label: Person
name: Albert Houssiau
summary:
Albert Houssiau (1924–2011) was a Belgian Catholic bishop and liturgical theologian who served as Bishop of Liège, contributing to both the Belgian Church's episcopal leadership and to scholarly reflection on the theology of Christian worship. Born in Liège, he was ordained a priest, pursued theological studies with particular attention to liturgy and patristics, and eventually became bishop of his home diocese.

Houssiau's scholarly work focused on sacramental and liturgical theology, an area of particular importance in the post-Vatican II Church as the council's liturgical reform required both implementation and theological reflection. His academic background informed his episcopal approach: he brought careful scholarly attention to the liturgical renewal of his diocese, ensuring that reform was accompanied by genuine theological understanding.

Liège's diocese had a distinguished intellectual and ecclesiastical history—it was the birthplace of the Corpus Christi feast instituted by Juliana of Liège in the thirteenth century, and its university had been a centre of Catholic scholarship since the medieval period. Houssiau's combination of scholarly acumen and pastoral commitment made him a fitting bishop for a diocese with such deep intellectual roots.
